title: Implement one-writer control leases across the room and session services
description:
Purpose:
Enforce the one-writer rule without collapsing terminal input into the room sequencer.

Scope:
- Add room-side acquire/release control operations and durable lease records.
- Grant or reject leases through the room actor.
- Make the session transport accept input only when authenticated with the current `lease_epoch`.
- Broadcast lease changes so non-holders update UI and stop typing.

Deliverables:
- Lease grant/revoke flow across room and session services.
- Lease-epoch validation in the data plane.
- Client-facing lease state updates.

Required test plan coverage:
- Lease acquisition and release coverage.
- Competing writers conflict coverage.
- Revocation-after-lease-change coverage.
- Input rejection coverage for stale lease epochs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Only one client at a time can type into a session.
- Lease state is authoritative, recoverable, and enforced by the session service.
- The room still sequences only lease control, not terminal bytes.

title: Implement a bootstrap-capable session backend and ordered output sequencing
description:
Purpose:
Satisfy the hard late-join requirement in the engineering plan by making the session backend capable of reconstructing current terminal state for a new subscriber.

Scope:
- Implement a bootstrap redraw path that emits a coherent redraw plus a live-stream anchor.
- Preserve per-session output ordering with explicit `output_seq` accounting.
- Use the local Ghostty tree and the zmx reference to shape a backend that can supervise long-lived terminal sessions without inventing a bespoke semantics-free process wrapper.
- Keep the backend pluggable so a better bootstrap source can replace the first implementation later.

Deliverables:
- Bootstrap-capable backend implementation or prototype adapter.
- Output log/anchor contract.
- Tests around join-after-output behavior.

Required test plan coverage:
- Late-join bootstrap coverage after a session has already produced output.
- Ordered live-stream continuation after bootstrap.
- Bootstrap correctness across resize and long-running session cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- A fresh client can reconstruct terminal state from bootstrap bytes plus the live stream.
- Session output remains strictly ordered per session.
- The architecture no longer hand-waves late join as future work.

title: Build SessionActor, SessionDirectory, and the PTY backend abstraction
description:
Purpose:
Define the server-side runtime boundary for terminal execution before transport and client subscription code accrete around an underspecified backend.

Scope:
- Implement `SessionActor` ownership of PTY lifecycle, output sequencing, subscriber set, status, and current size.
- Add a `SessionDirectory` for lookup and lifecycle management.
- Define a PTY backend abstraction that can support bootstrap-capable implementations later.
- Apply per-session resource limits and failure states as part of the actor lifecycle.

Deliverables:
- Session actor core.
- Session directory/service registry.
- PTY backend interface and resource-limit hooks.

Required test plan coverage:
- Session lifecycle tests for provisioning, running, exited, and failed states.
- Output sequence monotonicity tests.
- Resource-limit enforcement or failure-path coverage.
- Subscriber add/remove bookkeeping tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- The session service has one explicit authority boundary for PTY state.
- Later bootstrap, transport, and lease work can build on a real session actor instead of ad hoc per-socket state.
- PTY worker limits are part of the design from day one.

title: Implement the core GhosttySurfaceAdapter offscreen render contract
description:
Purpose:
Prove the host-side adapter contract for one embedded libghostty instance before broader composition or networking work starts.

Scope:
- Initialize one Ghostty surface with a canonical profile and grid size.
- Feed mock PTY output bytes into it.
- Render into an application-managed offscreen Metal texture, or the preferred documented fallback if direct render-to-texture is impossible.
- Expose a stable API for `init`, `ingest_output`, `resize`, `tick`, `request_render`, `latest_front_texture`, and `shutdown`.

Deliverables:
- `GhosttySurfaceAdapter` core implementation.
- Mock-PTY harness.
- Notes on unsupported behavior if any remain after the first proof.

Required test plan coverage:
- Adapter init/shutdown smoke.
- Mock output bytes produce a non-empty texture.
- Resize preserves subsequent rendering instead of corrupting output.

Acceptance criteria:
- One embedded surface can be created, fed bytes, rendered offscreen, resized, and torn down through the wrapper boundary.
- The host never needs Ghostty internals beyond the adapter contract.
- This bead materially retires the primary technical risk called out in the engineering plan.

title: Implement draw-when-needed frame scheduling across camera, texture, and timer updates
description:
Purpose:
Make redraw behavior event-driven so the app can stay smooth on interactive updates without burning frames when nothing changes.

Scope:
- Redraw on camera changes, room-surface changes, new published terminal textures, cursor/timer events, and overlay changes.
- Let the Metal view idle when nothing changed.
- Keep pacing compatible with variable-refresh displays instead of assuming a fixed cadence.
- Avoid tying the whole canvas frame loop to any single terminal surface's update timing.

Deliverables:
- `FrameScheduler` or equivalent invalidation coordinator.
- Wiring from surface publish events and timers into redraw requests.
- Tests around redraw reasons and idling.

Required test plan coverage:
- Camera-change redraw coverage.
- Texture-publish redraw coverage.
- Cursor timer invalidation coverage.
- Idle-no-op coverage when no state changed.

Acceptance criteria:
- The app draws when needed and idles when nothing changed.
- Terminal updates can lag a frame without stalling the whole compositor.
- Frame scheduling is explicit enough to debug missed updates and unnecessary redraw churn.

title: Bundle canonical render profiles and collaborative font assets
description:
Purpose:
Eliminate collaborative layout drift by making surface geometry derive from canonical shared profiles instead of per-user font settings.

Scope:
- Bundle the monospaced font assets used for collaborative surfaces.
- Define durable profile IDs with fixed font size, line height, cell metrics, padding, titlebar metrics, and theme IDs.
- Plumb profile IDs into room/client state and host initialization paths.
- Fail closed when an asset is missing or produces unexpected metrics.

Deliverables:
- Render-profile manifest/schema.
- Bundled font assets and load path.
- Metric validation and explicit error state.

Required test plan coverage:
- Profile load smoke for every bundled profile.
- Metric validation catches missing or drifted assets.
- Surface size derivation from `(cols, rows, profile_id, backing_scale)` is deterministic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Collaborative surfaces cannot silently fall back to arbitrary local font metrics.
- Room geometry and texture sizing can rely on canonical profile math.
- Missing collaborative assets fail explicitly instead of causing invisible divergence.

title: Fix DemoApp blank canvas presentation
Support effectively unbounded zoom in DemoApp
Model-check room invariants and snapshot replay equivalence
description:
Purpose:
Turn the room invariants in history/eng-plan.md into machine-checked contracts instead of relying on code review and hope.

Scope:
- Model `room_seq` monotonicity, `surface_id` uniqueness, dense total order over `stack_rank`, attachment uniqueness, active-lease uniqueness, and idempotent replay by `op_id`.
- Add a replay-equivalence check between the implementation and the formalized state machine where feasible.
- Wire the model run into the slower verification lane, not the fast pre-commit path.

Deliverables:
- TLA+ or equivalent model.
- Model-run documentation.
- Implementation fixtures tied back to the modelled invariants.

Required test plan coverage:
- Model check for small-state reorder and resize interleavings.
- Idempotent replay model cases.
- Snapshot + tail replay equivalence fixture tied to implementation tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- The control-plane invariants called out in the engineering plan are executable, not aspirational.
- Replay and ordering bugs have a dedicated regression surface outside ad hoc integration testing.
- The model is small enough to stay maintainable while still covering the high-risk semantics.

title: Implement an optimistic RoomReplica with op rebase and reject handling
description:
Purpose:
Keep spatial interactions feeling immediate while preserving the room actor as the source of durable truth.

Scope:
- Generate client `op_id` values.
- Apply pending ops optimistically to predicted room state.
- Rebase pending optimistic ops over authoritative accepts.
- Roll back or repair local prediction when the room rejects an op.

Deliverables:
- `RoomReplica` optimistic state machinery.
- Pending-op queue and rebase logic.
- Tests for accept/reject convergence.

Required test plan coverage:
- Optimistic move acceptance coverage.
- Optimistic resize/reorder rejection coverage.
- Pending-op rebase coverage across multiple outstanding ops.
- Duplicate authoritative event handling coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- The client has one explicit optimistic reconciliation path.
- Authoritative accepts and rejects converge to the same state the room actor holds.
- Later UI work can rely on fast local interactions without compromising durable truth.

title: Implement hit-testing and input arbitration for canvas, chrome, and terminal content
description:
Purpose:
Make control-plane vs data-plane routing a first-class client behavior instead of an emergent side effect of view layering.

Scope:
- Hit-test the topmost visible surface.
- Distinguish surface chrome from terminal content.
- Route camera pan/zoom, drag/resize/reorder, and lease requests to the control plane.
- Route typing, terminal-local wheel events, mouse reporting, and paste to the data plane.

Deliverables:
- Central `InputRouter` function/module.
- Surface hit-test helpers bound to draw order.
- Tests for routing decisions on overlapping surfaces and empty canvas regions.

Required test plan coverage:
- Topmost-surface hit-test coverage.
- Chrome-vs-content routing coverage.
- Empty-canvas routing to camera controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every pointer and keyboard event passes through one explicit routing decision.
- Canvas controls and terminal IO no longer depend on fragile host-view heuristics.
- Later multiplayer work can rely on a stable routing contract for leases and input delivery.

title: Pin the Ghostty vendor snapshot and enforce a wrapper-only embedding boundary
description:
Purpose:
Make the local `ghostty/` tree a pinned, wrapper-only dependency so upstream churn is isolated behind one compatibility boundary.

Scope:
- Record the pinned Ghostty snapshot contract used by V1.
- Create a local wrapper module that owns every raw libghostty call.
- Add compatibility checks that fail fast when the pinned embedding surface changes.
- Document what kinds of upstream changes require wrapper edits.

Deliverables:
- Wrapper boundary for libghostty access.
- Compatibility test target.
- Vendor/pinning documentation.

Required test plan coverage:
- Wrapper-only compile/link smoke against the pinned Ghostty tree.
- Compatibility tests catch missing or renamed upstream symbols used by the wrapper.
- Static scan or reviewable structure proves no non-wrapper code reaches directly into Ghostty embedding calls.

Acceptance criteria:
- The project has exactly one supported embedding boundary for Ghostty.
- Updating the vendor snapshot without wrapper work fails visibly.
- Later host/compositor/networking code depends only on the local wrapper API.

title: Align Zig and Metal style with ghostty reference
Separate presence and viewport state from the durable room log
description:
Purpose:
Keep ephemeral collaboration data out of the durable room log while still making it available to clients that need shared awareness.

Scope:
- Define presence payloads for camera position, viewport, cursor, and local selection hints.
- Relay presence through a separate service or channel from room WAL traffic.
- Ensure presence reconnect and expiration rules do not mutate durable room state.
- Surface control-lease display state without requiring WAL persistence for cursor/viewport chatter.

Deliverables:
- Presence channel contract.
- Client/server presence state handling.
- Tests for presence expiry and reconnect.

Required test plan coverage:
- Presence update fanout smoke.
- Presence reconnect and expiry coverage.
- Proof that presence messages do not affect room snapshot or journal content.

Acceptance criteria:
- Viewport and cursor chatter do not pollute durable room replay.
- Clients can still show collaborator awareness with bounded transient state.
- The room journal remains small and semantically clean.

title: Implement RoomActor journaling, snapshotting, and deterministic recovery
description:
Purpose:
Implement the single-writer room core that validates, sequences, persists, and recovers authoritative spatial state.

Scope:
- Validate incoming operations.
- Assign monotonically increasing `room_seq` values.
- Append accepted ops to the journal.
- Periodically write snapshots and recover from snapshot + tail replay.
- Keep side-effect hooks explicit instead of burying them in ad hoc code paths.

Deliverables:
- `RoomActor` core.
- Journal append and snapshot write/read paths.
- Recovery logic and replay tests.

Required test plan coverage:
- `room_seq` monotonicity tests.
- Snapshot + replay equivalence tests.
- Recovery from journal tail after snapshot tests.
- Duplicate `op_id` idempotence tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accepted room ops become durable before they are treated as authoritative.
- Recovery produces the same room state as uninterrupted execution.
- The room actor is a real authority boundary rather than a thin message relay.

title: Implement per-session transport, auth tokens, and reconnect anchors
description:
Purpose:
Give each subscribed terminal session its own simple, debuggable transport instead of hiding complexity behind an early multiplexing layer.

Scope:
- Implement a dedicated WebSocket or equivalent transport per subscribed terminal session.
- Authenticate each session connection with a scoped token and current lease epoch.
- Send bootstrap, output, status, and lease-revoked messages over the data plane.
- Support reconnect using output anchors and explicit status transitions.

Deliverables:
- Session transport protocol.
- Token/auth integration.
- Reconnect handling and diagnostics.

Required test plan coverage:
- Session auth success/failure coverage.
- Bootstrap + live message ordering coverage.
- Reconnect from a known anchor coverage.
- Lease-revoked message coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Session transport is session-local, ordered, and observable.
- Auth and reconnect semantics are explicit enough to debug in production.
- The data plane remains thin and separate from room sequencing logic.

title: Route keyboard, text, mouse, wheel, and paste input through Ghostty translation
description:
Purpose:
Keep terminal input semantics inside Ghostty, where terminal mode already lives, instead of duplicating translation logic in the host.

Scope:
- Route native key, text, mouse, wheel, and paste events into the adapter.
- Return PTY byte payloads for printable text, special keys, mouse reporting, bracketed paste, and wheel events that belong to terminal content.
- Define adapter APIs for selection, copy, and paste requests.
- Make the boundary between canvas-control events and terminal-data events explicit.

Deliverables:
- Adapter input-translation API.
- Host-side normalization for supported event classes.
- Automated coverage around representative translation scenarios.

Required test plan coverage:
- Printable text input produces PTY bytes.
- Representative special keys are translated through Ghostty instead of host lookup tables.
- Mouse reporting, wheel routing, and bracketed paste produce the expected presence or absence of output bytes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terminal input translation is adapter-owned and mode-aware.
- The host has a clear control-plane vs data-plane routing contract.
- Later networking work can send adapter-produced bytes directly to session sockets.

title: Switch DemoApp to drag pan and scroll zoom
Build headless GPU smoke and determinism test harness
description:
Purpose:
Turn the offscreen renderer into a real automated GPU verification harness with structural sampling and determinism checks, matching the test philosophy in history/demo.md.

Scope:
- Create a headless Metal test harness that renders to small offscreen textures and reads bytes back.
- Implement deterministic scene fixtures and helper assertions for interior pixel sampling.
- Cover pan, zoom, overlap order, empty scenes, resize, viewport-edge visibility, and repeated-render stability.
- Wire the GPU suite into the canonical verification command so it becomes part of the commit gate where feasible.

Important constraints from the plan:
- Do not attempt pixel-perfect CPU-vs-GPU golden comparisons.
- Sample pixels well inside rect interiors to avoid hardware edge-rule ambiguity.
- Keep images small and deterministic for fast local and CI execution.

Deliverables:
- GPU harness.
- Fixture scenes and sampling helpers.
- Automated GPU suite integrated into verification.

Required test plan coverage:
- G01 gpu_single_rect_interior.
- G02 gpu_overlap_painter_order.
- G03 gpu_pan_shifts_pixels.
- G04 gpu_zoom_scales_rect.
- G05 gpu_pan_zoom_combo.
- G06 gpu_empty_scene.
- G07 gpu_resize_consistency.
- G08 gpu_visible_set_boundary.
- G09 gpu_max_visible_rects_smoke.
- G10 gpu_repeated_render_stability.

Acceptance criteria:
- The GPU path has deterministic automated coverage for the behaviors most likely to regress during integration.
- Failures isolate transform/binding/order regressions without depending on brittle pixel-perfect goldens.
close_reason: Expanded the headless GPU harness to cover pan, zoom, combo, empty, resize, boundary, stress, and repeated-render determinism via offscreen readback

title: Finalize CI, packaging checks, and demo signoff gates
description:
Purpose:
Close the loop on packaging, CI, release/demo gating, and human signoff so the prototype is not just technically assembled but also repeatable and demoable.

Scope:
- Wire all automated verification lanes into CI using the canonical commands from the tooling bead.
- Add packaging/resource staging checks for app startup and metallib discovery.
- Define and automate the demo gate where practical, including release build and performance smoke.
- Capture the manual signoff matrix for interactive validation on an Apple Silicon target machine.
- Document the critical-path risks and mitigations as implemented reality, not just design intent.

Deliverables:
- CI workflow that runs the required lanes on macOS.
- Demo/release verification checklist.
- Manual signoff document/checklist.
- Packaging verification coverage.

Required test plan coverage:
- Commit gate remains green end-to-end.
- Demo gate includes release build, packaging verification, and performance smoke.
- Manual signoff checklist includes launch from clean checkout, metallib bundling, pan/zoom interaction, resize churn, long-running session stability, and sane stats output.

Acceptance criteria:
- The project has one documented path from clean checkout to demo signoff.
- Shipping/demo risk is visible through automated gates plus a bounded manual checklist.
close_reason: Added packaging verification, demo signoff docs, and CI jobs for both commit and demo gates

title: Add metrics and structured logs for room, session, Ghostty, and compositor paths
description:
Purpose:
Instrument the system so room, session, Ghostty, and compositor failures can be diagnosed from artifacts instead of guesswork.

Scope:
- Add metrics for room apply/journal/recovery, PTY latency and throughput, Ghostty render time, texture publish time, visible/occluded count, texture memory, frame time, and lease conflicts.
- Add structured logs carrying room, surface, session, client, op, and sequence identifiers.
- Keep the metric/log schema stable enough to use in replay and perf triage.

Deliverables:
- Metrics collection hooks.
- Structured log schema and emitters.
- Docs for reading the instrumentation during local debugging.

Required test plan coverage:
- Metric emission smoke for representative room and session flows.
- Structured log field presence checks for key events.
- Performance harness integration that consumes the new metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Core operations are observable without bespoke printf debugging.
- Logs and metrics carry enough identity to correlate room, session, and render events.
- Later replay, soak, and demo work can rely on the same instrumentation surface.

title: Define the durable room schema, op vocabulary, and persistence records
description:
Purpose:
Lock down the durable room data model before room-actor or client-replica logic starts inventing incompatible shapes.

Scope:
- Define room snapshots, room ops, session-attachment records, and control-lease records.
- Define the operation vocabulary for create, move, resize, reorder, close, attach, detach, acquire, and release.
- Define storage tables or persistence records for ops, snapshots, sessions, and leases.
- Keep room truth explicitly separate from ephemeral presence/viewport state.

Deliverables:
- Durable room schema and op definitions.
- Storage/migration plan for journal and snapshots.
- Serialization contracts shared by room service and client replica.

Required test plan coverage:
- Schema serialization round-trip tests.
- Op validation fixtures for required fields and illegal payloads.
- Snapshot compatibility tests for empty and populated rooms.

Acceptance criteria:
- The room model matches the architecture's flat-surface, cell-snapped, authoritative design.
- Later room, session, and client code can share one explicit vocabulary for spatial operations.
- Presence and viewport state are not accidentally baked into the durable schema.

title: Integrate room/session orchestration into a coherent multi-client surface lifecycle
description:
Purpose:
Connect the room plane and session plane into the actual user-facing multiplayer workflow.

Scope:
- Create surfaces through the room service.
- Start and attach sessions.
- Subscribe interested clients to attached sessions.
- Keep spatial edits, control-lease changes, and session failures synchronized into one coherent UI state.

Deliverables:
- Cross-service orchestration for create/attach/close flows.
- Client integration that reflects provisioning, attached, disconnected, error, and closing surface states.
- Tests around dual-plane lifecycle transitions.

Required test plan coverage:
- Create-surface to attached-session end-to-end coverage.
- Close-surface teardown coverage.
- Room-up/session-down and room-down/session-up failure-isolation coverage.
- Multi-view shared-surface coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- The product has one coherent multi-client surface lifecycle.
- Desired room state and actual session state reconcile cleanly into surface UI state.
- Control-plane and data-plane failures remain isolated while sharing the same surface model.

title: Harden PTY isolation, membership gating, token scope, and paste auditing
description:
Purpose:
Harden the server side so collaborative PTYs are not just functional but operationally defensible.

Scope:
- Apply per-session resource limits and isolation policy to PTY workers.
- Scope session tokens to one session and short lifetimes.
- Gate session subscribe/input by room membership and current lease state.
- Make clipboard and paste behavior explicit and auditable where server involvement exists.

Deliverables:
- Security/isolation policy implementation.
- Token-scope and membership enforcement.
- Audit hooks or docs for paste/clipboard-sensitive flows.

Required test plan coverage:
- Unauthorized session subscribe rejection coverage.
- Unauthorized input rejection coverage.
- Expired-token coverage.
- Membership-change invalidation coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- PTY access is bounded by room membership, token scope, and lease ownership.
- Resource limits are implemented rather than deferred to ops folklore.
- Sensitive input flows have explicit behavior and audit points.

title: Step 2: N=50 compositor and client scene core
description:
Step 2 from history/eng-plan.md.

Purpose:
Turn the current demo renderer into the bounded N=50 terminal compositor with the scene, pacing, and VRAM behavior needed by V1.

Scope:
- Refactor the scene around TerminalSurface geometry and profile-driven sizing.
- Replace placeholder rectangles with live terminal textures.
- Add input routing, CPU culling, z-order, conservative opaque occlusion skip, and draw-when-needed frame scheduling.
- Enforce the texture sizing and memory-budget policy from the plan.

Required test plan coverage:
- Visible-list and hit-test coverage for stacked terminal surfaces.
- Texture publish and frame-pacing tests under camera motion and timer-driven redraws.
- N=50 stress/performance checks with representative surface sizes.
- VRAM accounting checks against explicit thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- The client can pan and zoom a room of up to 50 representative terminal surfaces without architectural dead ends.
- Texture ownership, culling, and budget policy are encoded in code and tests, not just prose.
- Step 3 can build on a stable client-side spatial scene and compositor core.

title: Enforce canonical texture sizing, zoom policy, and VRAM budget accounting
description:
Purpose:
Encode the texture sizing and zoom policy from history/eng-plan.md so VRAM use and visual tradeoffs are deliberate.

Scope:
- Size textures from canonical surface point dimensions and device backing scale.
- Keep zoom-out filter behavior simple and mipmaps off by default.
- Track approximate texture memory by surface and by room.
- Add guardrails for oversized surfaces or room states that would blow the initial budget.

Deliverables:
- Texture-size calculation path shared by adapter/compositor code.
- Memory accounting stats.
- Policy checks or warnings for budget-breaking surfaces.

Required test plan coverage:
- Texture-size derivation coverage for representative profiles and backing scales.
- Memory accounting checks for front/back texture allocation.
- Budget-threshold checks for large-surface and many-surface scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
- Texture sizing follows the canonical formula from the engineering plan.
- Mipmaps are not silently enabled as a default escape hatch.
- The client can report and react to room states that exceed the intended V1 memory budget.

title: Build native MSL shader pipeline and metallib staging
description:
Purpose:
Prove the native Metal shader pipeline and artifact staging path independently of the full renderer. The plan is explicit that this should be native MSL compiled with xcrun metal/metallib, not a shader-codegen experiment.

Scope:
- Add rect_fill.metal (or equivalent) using the instanced rectangle vertex/fragment pipeline described in the plan.
- Teach the build to compile .metal to AIR and link AIR to .metallib.
- Stage the resulting .metallib where the host app and tests can load it predictably.
- Keep build.zig authoritative for Zig outputs and shader artifacts even if Xcode still owns the app target.

Implementation notes to preserve:
- The shader should stay intentionally small and native to MSL.
- The build graph should expose named steps for shader compilation and the broader CI path.
- Artifact staging must be deterministic and compatible with both local verification and CI.

Deliverables:
- MSL shader source.
- build.zig shader/custom steps.
- Staged .metallib output path contract.
- Packaging/load documentation for downstream consumers.

Required test plan coverage:
- I01 metal_compile_smoke.
- I02 metallib_build.
- I04 host_loads_metallib, at least as far as artifact discovery/staging can be verified without the full host shell.
- Inclusion in the commit gate from the verification foundation bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- A clean command builds the shader and staged metallib successfully.
- Downstream Metal shim and host tasks can treat metallib location as a stable contract.
close_reason: Added explicit shader build steps, deterministic staging paths, and compile/load verification for the native MSL pipeline

title: Step 3: room sequencer, WAL, and formal invariants
description:
Step 3 from history/eng-plan.md.

Purpose:
Build the authoritative control plane for durable spatial truth once the local rendering path is real.

Scope:
- Define the room schema, operation vocabulary, WAL, snapshots, and reconnect contracts.
- Implement sequencing, validation, rank rewrites, cell-snapped resize semantics, optimistic reconciliation, and presence separation.
- Add formal model coverage for sequence/order/idempotence invariants.

Required test plan coverage:
- Snapshot + replay equivalence tests.
- Accept/reject reconciliation tests for optimistic clients.
- Rank/order, ID uniqueness, and lease-record invariants.
- TLA+ or equivalent model-check runs in the slower verification lane.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accepted room ops are durable, replayable, and deterministic.
- Optimistic clients converge after accept or reject without corrupting the spatial scene.
- Formal invariants cover the control plane behaviors the architecture treats as non-negotiable.

title: Replace placeholder rect rendering with a live terminal texture compositor
description:
Purpose:
Replace the placeholder rect compositing path with live terminal textures while keeping the compositor intentionally simple.

Scope:
- Build one instance record per visible terminal quad.
- Bind published terminal textures and draw them with the existing Metal pipeline or its direct successor.
- Support minimal overlays needed for selection outlines, control-owner badges, or resize affordances.
- Keep the compositor focused on final presentation rather than terminal semantics.

Deliverables:
- Live terminal texture compositor path.
- Instance-data plumbing for terminal quads.
- Overlay hooks for minimal chrome.

Required test plan coverage:
- One-surface and overlap compositor coverage with real terminal textures.
- Correct z-order sampling for stacked surfaces.
- Overlay draw smoke that does not corrupt terminal content sampling.

Acceptance criteria:
- The renderer composes actual terminal textures instead of demo placeholders.
- Terminal semantics stay in Ghostty while the compositor stays a simple quad renderer.
- The live compositor is stable enough for culling, pacing, and stress work to build on it.

title: Upgrade or replace DemoApp as the host shell for embedded terminal surfaces
description:
Purpose:
Turn `host/DemoApp` into the actual host scaffold for the spatial terminal product, or replace it cleanly if the current shape fights the new architecture.

Scope:
- Decide whether to evolve DemoApp or swap in a replacement shell.
- Mount one or more embedded Ghostty surfaces through the adapter contract.
- Preserve artifact loading, resource staging, and host smoke coverage during the transition.
- Keep the repo’s fast verification path pointed at the real host shell.

Deliverables:
- Updated host-shell architecture note.
- Running host app that can present embedded terminal content.
- Packaging/resource verification updates if paths or targets move.

Required test plan coverage:
- Host launch smoke from clean build artifacts.
- Resource discovery for Ghostty-linked and app-bundled assets.
- Host interaction smoke for presenting at least one embedded terminal surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- The repo has one real host-shell path for V1; DemoApp is either upgraded or superseded, not left as a misleading dead-end.
- Host packaging and startup remain verified in automation.
- Step 2 work can build on a host that already knows how to present embedded terminal surfaces.

title: Add end-to-end multiplayer tests for late join, leases, reconnect, and failure isolation
description:
Purpose:
Make the Step 4 acceptance criteria measurable with end-to-end coverage instead of relying on manual multiplayer spot checks.

Scope:
- Stand up multi-client test scenarios that exercise shared viewing, lease exclusivity, late join bootstrap, reconnect, and failure isolation.
- Keep fixtures deterministic enough for repeated local and CI execution.
- Capture the cases most likely to regress when room/session code changes.

Deliverables:
- Multi-client end-to-end test harness.
- Deterministic scenario fixtures.
- Documentation for running the suite locally.

Required test plan coverage:
- Shared-view / one-writer coverage.
- Late-join bootstrap coverage.
- Room reconnect and session reconnect coverage.
- Control-plane outage with live session, and session outage with live room, coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- The dual-plane multiplayer behavior is exercised automatically.
- Step 4 exit criteria are proven by tests, not recollection.
- Regression risk on the highest-level user workflow is materially reduced.

title: Build the N=50 compositor stress harness and performance checks
description:
Purpose:
Prove the Step 2 exit criteria with a stress harness that matches the architecture target instead of assuming the compositor will scale.

Scope:
- Exercise up to 50 representative surfaces using dummy and, where practical, real terminal textures.
- Measure visible count, occluded count, frame time, publish latency, and approximate texture memory.
- Capture scenarios with heavy overlap, mixed sizes, camera motion, and timer-driven terminal churn.
- Keep results reproducible enough for CI/demo comparison.

Deliverables:
- Stress/performance harness.
- Captured thresholds for acceptable local/demo behavior.
- Docs for how to run and interpret the harness.

Required test plan coverage:
- `N=50` mixed-size scene smoke.
- Heavy-overlap scene smoke.
- Camera pan/zoom stress run.
- Multi-surface publish churn run.

Acceptance criteria:
- Step 2 has measurable exit criteria instead of subjective “seems fast” judgments.
- The client surfaces memory/bandwidth pressure before Step 4 multiplies the load with networking.
- Performance regressions can be compared against a stable harness.

title: Expand pre-commit and CI gates for the Ghostty-backed architecture
description:
Purpose:
Expand the existing fast local gate so the Ghostty-backed architecture stays covered by pre-commit instead of drifting into CI-only verification.

Scope:
- Keep `.githooks/pre-commit` authoritative.
- Add Ghostty-wrapper, host-shell, compositor, room, and multiplayer checks as they become real.
- Preserve a fast local gate and a slower demo/release gate, but make the fast gate cover real correctness risk.
- Keep failure output specific enough for local debugging.

Deliverables:
- Updated `scripts/verify-commit.sh` / related scripts.
- Documentation of fast vs slow lanes.
- One intentionally induced failure case documented or scripted.

Required test plan coverage:
- Hook rejects a commit when a representative Ghostty/compositor/room test fails.
- Hook passes on a clean tree.
- New V1 verification entrypoints are discoverable from docs and README.

Acceptance criteria:
- Later beads can rely on one authoritative fast gate.
- Tests continue running on pre-commit throughout the architecture transition.
- Developers do not need tribal knowledge to know which checks are required before commit.

title: Establish pinned toolchain, doctor command, and pre-commit verification gate
description:
Why first:
The plan explicitly calls for exact tool pinning, repeatable gates, and a commit gate that automatically runs formatting, build, tests, shader compilation, GPU smoke coverage, and host integration checks. This must land before implementation branches start, otherwise every later stream can drift on tooling and quality bars.

Scope:
- Pin the exact Zig version and the expected Xcode / Command Line Tools version for this prototype.
- Add a fast-fail doctor/verification entrypoint that validates required tools and versions.
- Install repo-managed pre-commit automation so local commits automatically run the required verification suite.
- Define the authoritative verification commands for format, build, unit, integration, GPU, and host-boundary checks.
- Document what runs in the fast commit gate versus the slower demo gate.

Implementation notes:
- Prefer repo-managed hooks or an installer script so the hook is reproducible across machines.
- The hook should run the whole required commit-gate suite, not just formatting.
- If runtime cost forces a split, define a single canonical wrapper command that the hook executes and keep the command graph in version control.
- The verification suite should include shader compile/metallib checks early, because shader pipeline drift is one of the primary technical risks.

Deliverables:
- Pinned toolchain policy in-repo.
- Pre-commit hook setup and documentation.
- Doctor command / script.
- Canonical verification entrypoint(s) used by both humans and CI.
- Initial CI lane shell or equivalent automation stub wired to the same commands.

Required test plan coverage:
- Run and document the full commit gate.
- Prove the hook blocks a commit on at least one induced failure.
- Prove the hook passes on a clean tree.
- Verify doctor failure messaging when Zig or xcrun/metal/metallib is missing or on the wrong version.

Acceptance criteria:
- A fresh collaborator can install the hook and run one command to execute the full verification suite.
- A commit without passing verification is rejected locally.
- Later implementation beads can depend on this instead of inventing their own workflows.
close_reason: Implemented pinned toolchain policy, doctor command, managed pre-commit hook, and canonical verification suite

title: Implement pure Zig camera math, scene store, and visible-set core
description:
Purpose:
Build the pure Zig logic that should be correct before any GPU debugging begins: affine camera math, visible-set construction, painter's-order preservation, and scene data handling.

Scope:
- Implement the y-down canvas camera model using a single affine matrix source of truth.
- Implement screen<->canvas transforms and anchor-preserving zoom behavior.
- Implement the master scene store and per-frame visible-set builder.
- Preserve painter's order by array order.
- Handle capacity overflow explicitly instead of silently dropping rects.
- Keep this path pure Zig and independent of Metal/Swift.

Important constraints from the plan:
- The visible set uploaded to the GPU is a filtered per-frame array, not the full scene.
- Zoom-around-cursor should be expressed with matrix composition, not ad hoc pan math.
- This layer should be deterministic and small enough to serve as the logic oracle for later integration work.

Deliverables:
- Camera math module.
- Visible-set / culling module.
- Scene storage and replacement semantics sufficient for unit testing.
- Unit test suite for geometry, transforms, order preservation, and capacity behavior.

Required test plan coverage:
- U01 camera_roundtrip.
- U02 zoom_anchor_preserved.
- U03 zoom_clamped.
- U04 pan_updates_camera.
- U05 rect_contains_edges.
- U06 visible_set_basic.
- U07 visible_set_preserves_order.
- U08 visible_set_capacity_error.
- U09 replace_rects_copies_input if scene replacement scaffolding lands here.

Acceptance criteria:
- The pure Zig logic passes its unit suite without any Metal dependency.
- Transform roundtrips and visible-set semantics match the detailed expectations in history/demo.md.
close_reason: Implemented camera math, scene storage, visible-set builder, and unit coverage for transform and culling semantics

title: Implement shared-queue double-buffered texture publish for terminal surfaces
description:
Purpose:
Implement the steady-state texture ownership model from the engineering plan so the compositor never samples a texture Ghostty is still writing.

Scope:
- Add per-surface front/back texture state and generation tracking.
- Commit adapter renders through the shared render authority.
- Swap only after GPU completion.
- Keep the previous front texture visible during lag or resize reallocation.

Deliverables:
- Per-surface texture state implementation.
- Publish/swap protocol.
- Resize-safe handoff behavior.

Required test plan coverage:
- Front texture remains stable while a back render is in flight.
- Completion-triggered publish increments the generation exactly once per successful frame.
- Resize keeps the old front texture composable until a new-size frame is published.

Acceptance criteria:
- The host has one race-free publish protocol for terminal textures.
- Staleness is preferred over compositor stalls when terminal renders lag.
- Later multi-surface composition can rely on coherent texture generations.

title: Step 1: Ghostty bridge and embedded terminal proof
description:
Step 1 from history/eng-plan.md.

Purpose:
Prove the Ghostty embedding boundary before the rest of the system depends on it.

Scope:
- Pin and wrap the Ghostty dependency.
- Establish canonical collaborative render profiles and font assets.
- Prove offscreen embedded libghostty can ingest output, translate input, render into publishable textures, and run inside the real host shell.
- Keep the pre-commit path authoritative as Ghostty-backed tests land.

Required test plan coverage:
- Host launch smoke with one embedded terminal surface.
- Adapter init/ingest/render/resize/shutdown coverage.
- Keyboard, mouse, paste, selection, cursor timer, and IME-sensitive checks for embedded mode.
- Commit-gate coverage for the new Ghostty-backed path.

Acceptance criteria:
- The project has a real embedded-terminal path that can be treated as the shipping architecture base, not a hidden-window prototype.
- The host/compositor code depends only on a local Ghostty compatibility layer.
- Any missing embedded behaviors are turned into explicit blocking beads before later steps assume them.

title: Align demo Zig/Metal bridge with ghostty patterns
Demo prototype execution plan from history/demo.md
description:
Source: history/demo.md.

Goal:
Turn the demo plan into an executable implementation backlog for the Apple Silicon macOS prototype: Zig engine, native MSL shader pipeline, thin Objective-C Metal shim, SwiftUI/MTKView shell, and a verification strategy that makes correctness and demo readiness measurable.

Success criteria:
- A macOS app embeds MTKView in SwiftUI and presents a continuously rendered infinite 2D canvas.
- Zig owns camera math, visible-set construction, render dispatch decisions, engine memory, and exported C ABI.
- GPU rendering uses a native MSL instanced rectangle pipeline compiled to a staged .metallib.
- Panning and zooming are immediate and deterministic.
- The implementation is guarded by automated unit, integration, GPU, and host-boundary tests, plus manual signoff gates.

Non-goals:
- Text rendering.
- Selection, hit-testing, or editing tools.
- Intel Mac support.
- A production asset pipeline.
- SPIR-V or shader codegen experiments that replace direct MSL for this demo.

Execution model:
- Make the verification / pre-commit foundation land first.
- After that, split work so ABI/build, pure Zig engine logic, and shader/build integration can proceed in parallel.
- Keep Metal integration and host-shell work blocked on the minimum required predecessors instead of serializing the whole plan.

Verification umbrella:
- Commit gate: formatting, build, unit tests, C ABI link smoke, shader compile/metallib build, GPU offscreen smoke tests, host-shell integration tests.
- Demo gate: release build, packaging verification, performance smoke, manual signoff matrix.
close_reason: Implemented the executable backlog from history/demo.md through tooling, engine, shader, bridge, GPU, host, and demo gate work

title: Wire demo, soak, and release verification around the real product path
description:
Purpose:
Close the loop on verification so the real product path stays demoable and regressions are caught before they ship.

Scope:
- Keep the fast pre-commit gate focused and mandatory.
- Define the slower demo/release gate around N=50 performance, multiplayer end-to-end, replay tooling, and packaging/startup checks.
- Add a bounded long-running soak path for session churn and reconnect behavior.
- Document manual signoff that cannot reasonably be automated.

Deliverables:
- Updated verification scripts and CI wiring for fast vs slow lanes.
- Demo/soak checklist and docs.
- Packaging/startup checks pointed at the real host shell.

Required test plan coverage:
- Fast gate remains green on a clean tree and includes core Ghostty/compositor/room coverage.
- Slow gate includes N=50 stress, multiplayer end-to-end, replay-tool smoke, and packaging/startup checks.
- Soak run definition for long-lived sessions and reconnect churn.

Acceptance criteria:
- The project has one documented path from clean checkout to demo signoff.
- Pre-commit remains intact while the slower gates expand around it.
- Release/demo readiness is measured against the actual product architecture, not the old rect-demo scaffold.

title: Implement client session subscription, bootstrap replay, and failure-isolated surface states
description:
Purpose:
Connect the data plane to the client-side Ghostty manager so session subscriptions produce real terminal pixels and real failure states.

Scope:
- Open a session transport for each subscribed surface.
- Create a fresh adapter on subscribe or reconnect.
- Feed bootstrap bytes, then live output bytes, into the adapter.
- Surface disconnected/error overlays without tearing down the rest of the canvas.

Deliverables:
- Client `SessionClient` and `GhosttyManager` integration.
- Bootstrap-then-live ingest path.
- Failure-state UI contract for disconnected or failed sessions.

Required test plan coverage:
- Subscribe/bootstrap/live ingest coverage.
- Reconnect with fresh adapter coverage.
- Failed-session overlay coverage.
- Unsubscribe/teardown coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Client-side session subscription produces a coherent terminal surface.
- Session failures degrade one surface instead of taking down the whole canvas.
- Bootstrap and reconnect behavior are explicit and testable.

title: Step 4: networked PTY sessions and multiplayer integration
description:
Step 4 from history/eng-plan.md.

Purpose:
Add the terminal session service and multiplayer behavior after the local render path and room durability are both proven.

Scope:
- Build the session actor, PTY backend abstraction, bootstrap-capable subscribe flow, and per-session transport.
- Enforce one-writer control leases without routing terminal bytes through the room sequencer.
- Integrate client-side bootstrap replay, live stream ingestion, reconnect handling, and failure-isolated surface states.
- Prove late join, multi-view, and plane-independent failures end to end.

Required test plan coverage:
- Bootstrap + live-stream correctness for a joining client.
- Lease exclusivity and revocation tests.
- Room reconnect and session reconnect coverage.
- Multi-client end-to-end tests for dual-plane failure isolation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Multiple clients can observe the same terminal while only the current lease holder can type.
- A joining client receives a coherent redraw plus ordered live output.
- Control-plane outages and session-plane outages degrade independently.

title: Spatial terminal canvas V1 execution plan from history/eng-plan.md
description:
Source: history/eng-plan.md, with implementation constraints informed by the local ghostty vendor tree and the zmx session-persistence reference.

Goal:
Turn the architecture in history/eng-plan.md into an execution backlog that ships a macOS-native collaborative spatial terminal canvas with a dual-plane design: authoritative durable room state for spatial truth, direct PTY byte streams for terminal IO, embedded libghostty instances as local terminal engines, and a simple Metal quad compositor for final presentation.

Execution order:
- Step 1 proves Ghostty offscreen embedding and host integration before more architecture is built on top of it.
- Step 2 proves N=50 compositor behavior, culling, pacing, and VRAM discipline using real terminal textures.
- Step 3 builds the authoritative room sequencer, WAL, snapshots, optimistic reconciliation, and formal invariants.
- Step 4 adds the session service, PTY bootstrap/reconnect behavior, control leases, and multi-client integration.
- Step 5 hardens observability, replay, security, and release/demo gates.

Backlog policy:
- Preserve or improve the repo-managed pre-commit gate as each stream lands.
- Treat host/DemoApp as a disposable scaffold: reuse it where it helps, but rewrite or replace it if that is the cleanest path to match history/eng-plan.md.
- Keep all raw libghostty access behind a local compatibility layer because the upstream API is not a stable standalone embedding contract.

title: Implement SwiftUI/MTKView host shell and normalized input bridge
description:
Purpose:
Build the macOS host shell once the engine, ABI, and Metal path are proven: SwiftUI wrapper, MTKView lifecycle, and normalized input delivery into Zig.

Scope:
- Add the SwiftUI/AppKit bridge using NSViewRepresentable.
- Create/configure MTKView, delegate/coordinator, device/pixel format, and draw callback wiring.
- Pass drawable size, current drawable texture, pan deltas, and zoom events into the engine.
- Support precise vs coarse scrolling and provide a non-gesture zoom fallback.
- Target Apple Silicon / ProMotion-friendly behavior consistent with the plan.

Important constraints from the plan:
- Swift is the host shell only; engine logic stays in Zig.
- The shell should not block on reinventing build ownership beyond consuming staged artifacts.
- Gestures should supplement, not replace, conventional zoom input.

Deliverables:
- SwiftUI wrapper and MTKView integration.
- Input event normalization and zoom fallback path.
- Host-side artifact/resource loading for the engine and metallib.

Required test plan coverage:
- H01 mtkview_delegate_calls_engine.
- H02 drawable_size_propagates.
- H03 scroll_pan_propagates.
- H04 magnify_zoom_propagates.
- H05 fallback_zoom_path.
- H06 precise_vs_coarse_scroll_normalization.

Acceptance criteria:
- The host shell can drive the real engine continuously and route user input predictably.
- Input and resize behavior match the rules laid out in history/demo.md.
close_reason: Added the SwiftUI/MTKView host shell, input normalization, real engine dylib loading, and host-side tests

title: Implement thin Objective-C Metal bridge and offscreen render spike
description:
Purpose:
Attack the highest technical risk directly: prove Zig can drive Metal through a thin Objective-C shim and render deterministically into an offscreen texture using the ABI and shader artifacts established earlier.

Scope:
- Implement the tiny Objective-C Metal bridge that wraps the minimal final API calls into Metal.
- Create pipeline state, render pass setup, buffer binding, instanced draw call, command submission, and texture presentation/readback support needed for tests.
- Drive the shim from Zig using the exported engine-facing interface and ABI types.
- Start with offscreen rendering and deterministic test scenes before any SwiftUI shell work.

Important constraints from the plan:
- Keep Objective-C as a thin, replaceable FFI membrane only; scene logic and render decisions remain in Zig.
- Use the hardware rasterizer via instanced vertex/fragment rendering, not a brute-force compute rasterizer.
- The spike should prove correct ABI layout, linking, and deterministic pixel sampling on a small texture such as 64x64.

Deliverables:
- Objective-C bridge implementation and headers.
- Zig-side render integration calling through the bridge.
- Offscreen render harness sufficient for GPU tests.
- Basic stats/error plumbing needed to debug failures.

Required test plan coverage:
- I03 c_header_link_smoke if not already complete.
- I05 invalid_metallib_path_fails_cleanly.
- GPU harness prerequisites for G01-G10.
- Deterministic offscreen render proof with at least one tiny scene.

Acceptance criteria:
- Zig can initialize the renderer, render via the bridge into an offscreen texture, and produce deterministic sampled pixels.
- The integration risk of Zig + Metal + ObjC is materially retired before host-shell work begins.
close_reason: Implemented Objective-C Metal bridge, offscreen renderer path, metallib-path init, and deterministic GPU readback tests

title: Add CPU culling, z-order sorting, and conservative opaque occlusion skip
description:
Purpose:
Keep the compositor bounded and debug-friendly by doing visibility and most occlusion work on the CPU, as the engineering plan calls for.

Scope:
- Compute the current world-space view rect.
- Reject surfaces outside the view rect.
- Preserve painter's order by `stack_rank`.
- Add conservative opaque occlusion skip without partial rectangle splitting.

Deliverables:
- Visible-surface builder for terminal surfaces.
- Optional coarse opaque-coverage tracker.
- Tests for deterministic skip behavior.

Required test plan coverage:
- Frustum culling coverage at viewport boundaries.
- Painter's-order preservation for visible survivors.
- Fully-covered opaque-surface skip coverage.
- No false skip when a surface is only partially covered or translucent.

Acceptance criteria:
- CPU culling and optional opaque occlusion are deterministic and easy to reason about.
- The compositor uploads only the visible list instead of every surface in the room.
- Overdraw mitigation stays intentionally conservative rather than turning into a complex scene engine.

title: Implement stack-rank rewrite and cell-snapped resize semantics in the room
description:
Purpose:
Encode the room-specific semantics that matter for collaboration instead of leaving them as UI-only behaviors.

Scope:
- Maintain dense `stack_rank` ordering across create, reorder, and close operations.
- Make resize authoritative in `(cols, rows)` rather than arbitrary pixels.
- Validate profile IDs and session-attachment constraints in room operations.
- Keep move/resize/reorder semantics deterministic for replay and optimistic reconciliation.

Deliverables:
- Rank-rewrite and resize semantics inside room validation/apply logic.
- Tests for deterministic ordering and cell-snapped resize behavior.
- Error cases for illegal ranks, sizes, or attachment transitions.

Required test plan coverage:
- Dense-rank rewrite tests for reorder and close.
- Cell-snapped resize op tests.
- Invalid-rank and invalid-size rejection tests.
- Session-attachment state-transition tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Room operations preserve one total surface order and one canonical terminal size per surface.
- Reorder and resize outcomes are deterministic under replay.
- Clients do not get to invent private pixel sizes that diverge from room truth.

title: Step 5: observability, security, and demo hardening
description:
Step 5 from history/eng-plan.md.

Purpose:
Harden the system for debugging, operations, and demoability once the primary execution path exists.

Scope:
- Add metrics, structured logs, and offline replay tools.
- Harden PTY-worker isolation, token scope, membership gating, and paste/clipboard auditing.
- Wire fast-vs-slow verification, soak coverage, and demo signoff around the real product path.

Required test plan coverage:
- Metrics/log assertions on representative room and session flows.
- Replay-tool golden cases for room and session traces.
- Security policy checks around session auth and lease enforcement.
- Demo and soak verification lane definitions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Operators can diagnose room/session/compositor failures from captured artifacts.
- PTY access is explicitly bounded by auth, membership, and lease state.
- The product has a documented path from clean checkout to demo signoff without bypassing pre-commit discipline.

title: Implement authoritative resize side effects and desired-vs-actual reconciliation
description:
Purpose:
Make authoritative resize a cross-service contract instead of a local preview that can silently diverge from PTY state.

Scope:
- Take durable `(cols, rows)` commits from the room service.
- Emit idempotent resize side effects to the session actor.
- Apply PTY `winsize` changes only after authoritative room commit.
- Surface desired-vs-actual lag explicitly so the client can show progress or stale state.

Deliverables:
- Room-to-session resize side-effect path.
- Session resize application and acknowledgement handling.
- Client-visible lag/error state if resize application is delayed or fails.

Required test plan coverage:
- Authoritative resize side-effect coverage.
- Idempotent repeated-resize coverage.
- Lagging-session desired-vs-actual reconciliation coverage.
- Resize-after-reconnect coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terminal size is authoritative in the room and eventually reflected in the PTY backend.
- Resize lag is explicit and recoverable rather than hidden.
- Clients do not diverge permanently on session size.

title: Refactor the client scene into a flat TerminalSurface store
description:
Purpose:
Refactor the client scene around durable `TerminalSurface` state instead of the current demo-specific rect store.

Scope:
- Implement a flat SoA-style surface store with IDs, session IDs, world position, `cols`, `rows`, `profile_id`, `stack_rank`, and flags.
- Derive outer geometry from canonical render profiles.
- Provide efficient lookup, replacement, and ordered iteration for rendering and hit-testing.
- Keep the scene representation aligned with the room schema from the engineering plan.

Deliverables:
- `SurfaceManager` or equivalent SoA storage.
- Deterministic geometry derivation helpers.
- Unit coverage for scene mutation and order preservation.

Required test plan coverage:
- Surface insert/update/remove coverage.
- Geometry derivation from profile + grid size.
- Dense draw-order maintenance when stack ranks change.

Acceptance criteria:
- The client scene model matches the durable TerminalSurface concept from the plan.
- Rendering and networking layers can share one surface-state shape instead of translating ad hoc demo structs.
- The scene remains small, deterministic, and easy to serialize or reconcile.

title: Prove selection, clipboard, IME, cursor timers, and resize behavior in embedded mode
description:
Purpose:
Prove the embedded mode behaves like a real terminal and not just a byte-to-pixels demo.

Scope:
- Verify selection/copy semantics in embedded mode.
- Verify paste requests, cursor blink or timer-driven redraws, and resize behavior.
- Verify IME/text-services behavior and secure-input-adjacent flows early enough to uncover blockers while the wrapper is still malleable.
- Split any discovered blockers into follow-on issues instead of leaving them implicit.

Deliverables:
- Embedded behavior verification matrix.
- Automated coverage where feasible.
- Bounded manual checks for native behaviors that cannot be automated reliably.

Required test plan coverage:
- Selection copy smoke.
- Paste-request smoke.
- Cursor blink/timer invalidation smoke.
- IME/manual composition checklist on Apple Silicon.
- Password-prompt or secure-input-adjacent checklist if automation is impractical.

Acceptance criteria:
- Embedded Ghostty behavior is known for the features that would disqualify the product if broken.
- Remaining platform gaps are explicit blocking issues, not assumptions.
- Later phases do not proceed under a false assumption that embedded mode is feature-complete.

title: Build offline room and session replay tooling
description:
Purpose:
Make hard bugs replayable offline instead of requiring live reproduction across multiple services and clients.

Scope:
- Build room replay from snapshot + journal.
- Build session replay from bootstrap bytes + live output log.
- Provide fixtures and tooling to feed replays back into local debugging or regression tests.
- Tie replay identity to the structured logs and metrics added elsewhere.

Deliverables:
- Room replay tool.
- Session replay tool.
- Replay fixture format and docs.

Required test plan coverage:
- Room replay reproduces a known room state fixture.
- Session replay reproduces a known bootstrap + output stream fixture.
- Replay artifacts can seed at least one regression test path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Engineers can replay the two main planes offline.
- Replay tooling is good enough to shorten debugging loops on room/session regressions.
- Observability artifacts are no longer write-only data.

title: Add CPU reference renderer, engine state machine, and no-allocation guarantees
description:
Purpose:
Add a CPU-side renderer and engine-memory/state scaffolding so transform logic, painter's order, and steady-state allocation guarantees can be validated before GPU bring-up.

Scope:
- Implement the CPU reference renderer used for sampled interior-pixel correctness checks.
- Implement engine-owned storage semantics for replace_rects and steady-state no-allocation behavior after init.
- Add the engine state machine shell needed to reject invalid call ordering deterministically.
- Add snapshot/double-buffered camera state or equivalent render-snapshot logic if this is the cleanest place to validate thread-safe camera handling.

Important constraints from the plan:
- The CPU renderer is not a pixel-perfect GPU oracle; it validates interior samples and painter's order, not hardware edge rules.
- After engine_init, the steady-state render-prep path should perform no heap allocations.
- Caller-owned rect memory must be copied into engine-owned storage.

Deliverables:
- CPU reference renderer.
- Allocation/accounting test harness.
- Engine state machine baseline and error code coverage.
- Concurrency-safe camera snapshot strategy, or the test scaffolding that proves it later in engine integration.

Required test plan coverage:
- U09 replace_rects_copies_input.
- U13 cpu_reference_single_rect.
- U14 cpu_reference_overlap.
- U15 cpu_reference_pan_zoom.
- U16 engine_state_machine.
- U17 steady_state_no_alloc.
- U18 camera_snapshot_isolation.
- I05 invalid_metallib_path_fails_cleanly can partially land here if init error plumbing exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- The CPU renderer is good enough to validate sampled interior pixels and overlap order.
- Allocation and state-machine regressions are caught in automated tests.
- This bead leaves later GPU tests with a trustworthy non-GPU logic baseline.
close_reason: Added CPU reference renderer, state-machine coverage, and steady-state render-prep validation without extra allocations

title: Integrate engine runtime, camera snapshotting, and frame-state ownership
description:
Purpose:
Integrate the pure Zig engine logic with the render path so camera updates, visible-set construction, render dispatch, frame stats, and ownership rules all operate together under the exported API.

Scope:
- Connect engine_init/resize/pan/zoom/replace_rects/render/get_stats/error APIs to real engine state.
- Pre-allocate engine-owned buffers and eliminate steady-state heap allocation after init.
- Snapshot pending camera state into the active frame state at render start.
- Rebuild visible_rects per frame and bind the resulting instance data to the renderer.
- Surface stats and deterministic error handling through the C ABI.

Important constraints from the plan:
- Input functions and render may run concurrently, so render must operate on a stable snapshot.
- Replace_rects must copy caller memory.
- The render path should operate on visible_rects, not all_rects.
- Frame stats should report at least total rects, visible rects, and viewport dimensions.

Deliverables:
- Integrated engine runtime.
- Buffer ownership / lifetime handling.
- Camera snapshot logic.
- Frame stats and error message plumbing.
- Tests covering integrated state behavior.

Required test plan coverage:
- U09, U16, U17, U18 if not already complete.
- I06 engine_render_before_init_fails.
- Readiness for G03-G09 where camera and visible-set behavior affect GPU output.

Acceptance criteria:
- The engine API is no longer a shell; it drives real runtime state and render submissions.
- Render-time behavior is deterministic under concurrent input updates.
close_reason: Integrated pending and active camera state, render-time visible-set rebuilds, frame stats, and runtime ownership checks through the engine API

title: Define shared ABI, exported C API, and compile-time layout guarantees
description:
Purpose:
Lock down the ABI contract before the real engine/Metal integration work expands. The demo plan depends on explicit extern structs, packed color representation, compile-time layout asserts, and a narrow exported C API.

Scope:
- Define shared GPU-facing structs such as CameraUniform and Rect with explicit ABI layout.
- Define the exported engine C ABI surface, status codes, config, stats, and error-reporting contract.
- Generate or stage the C header consumed by the host side and link-smoke harness.
- Add compile-time assertions for size, offset, and alignment invariants.
- Encode the thread-affinity and ownership rules in comments/docs near the API.

Implementation details to preserve from history/demo.md:
- Use extern structs for ABI-visible data.
- Use *anyopaque for foreign Metal handles.
- Keep Rect at a 16-byte multiple, with packed RGBA8 color and explicit padding.
- Keep CameraUniform as the uploaded 3x2 affine transform plus viewport dimensions.
- Reject vague type naming that obscures ownership semantics.

Deliverables:
- Shared Zig type definitions.
- Exported API declarations and generated header.
- Compile-time layout tests/assertions.
- Minimal C harness target that includes the generated header.

Required test plan coverage:
- U10 camera_uniform_layout.
- U11 rect_layout.
- U12 color_pack_unpack_roundtrip.
- I03 c_header_link_smoke.
- I06 engine_render_before_init_fails can start here if the state machine shell exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- The header is generated/staged reproducibly.
- ABI structs match the documented layout exactly.
- A tiny external C consumer can compile and link against the exported surface.

title: Build the RoomGateway snapshot-tail API and reconnect protocol
description:
Purpose:
Expose the room authority to clients through one reconnect-friendly API instead of pushing transport concerns into every consumer.

Scope:
- Serve room snapshots and tail ops after a known `room_seq`.
- Broadcast accepted ops and rejects to connected clients.
- Define reconnect semantics that rebuild the client replica deterministically.
- Keep presence or session traffic out of the durable room stream.

Deliverables:
- `RoomGateway` or equivalent transport boundary.
- Snapshot/tail replay protocol.
- Reconnect handling and tests.

Required test plan coverage:
- Cold-join snapshot load coverage.
- Tail replay from a known `room_seq` coverage.
- Reconnect after missed ops coverage.
- Reject-delivery coverage for invalid client ops.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clients can recover room truth from one explicit gateway contract.
- Reconnect does not require bespoke state repair code in the client.
- The room transport stays focused on authoritative spatial state.
